name: Sophia C.
highlight: Asked who I was actually performing for
comment: I’ve spent the last six months constantly feeling like I’m falling behind everyone else my age, even though on paper things look fine. Did the audit prompt on page 9 two nights ago. It didn’t try to fix me or give me advice—it just asked who I was actually performing for. That question has been sitting in my chest ever since.

name: Marcus V.
highlight: Calling you out to your face
comment: I'm the guy who always talks about what he’s 'about to do' but quietly avoids the daily work. The prompt on self-betrayal made me write out the exact promises I broke to myself this past week alone. It stung, but in a good way. Like someone finally calling you out to your face.

name: Julian C.
comment: I usually get bored of these things by day two. But having just one page to read and one question to answer makes it impossible to hide. It’s kept my head clear the past couple mornings.

name: Alex R.
comment: The section on the desire to be liked hit a nerve. I realized how much energy I waste saying yes to things I hate just so people think I'm easygoing. Filled out the response yesterday and felt an immediate sense of relief. It’s like having an older sibling who cuts through all your rationalizations.

name: David S.
comment: Expected another preachy PDF. It’s not that at all. It’s just quiet, uncomfortable truths about why we avoid being alone with our thoughts. Really needed this.

name: Elena R.
highlight: Closing a tab in my brain
comment: Read page 22 on letting go of past versions of yourself on Sunday night. I’ve been holding onto an identity that expired two years ago and wondering why I felt stuck. Writing that out on paper felt like closing a tab in my brain that’s been open forever.
